title: One Neuron, Two Ways to Lose Axons

scenes.tts: How can a neuron cut off a branch with enzymes that could kill the whole cell? Pruning means removing an axon branch from a neuron that survives. The enzymes are caspases. Caspases are proteases that dismantle a cell during apoptosis. Yet a neuron can use them on one axon and live. Mouse sympathetic neurons show how.
scenes.visual: A neuron with three branches; one branch is cut away by caspases while the cell body lives.
scenes.narration: How can a neuron cut off a branch with enzymes that could kill the whole cell? Pruning means removing an axon branch from a neuron that survives. The enzymes are caspases. Caspases are proteases that dismantle a cell during apoptosis. Yet a neuron can use them on one axon and live. Mouse sympathetic neurons show how.

scenes.tts: Researchers built a chamber with two compartments. The cell bodies of mouse sympathetic neurons sat in one compartment. Their axons grew through narrow grooves into the other. Many sympathetic neurons send branches toward targets that make N G F. Both sides held N G F, a trophic factor, which is a growth factor supplied by the target. This setup lets them remove N G F from the axons alone.
scenes.visual: Two-compartment chamber builds: bodies left, axons through grooves right, NGF dots on both sides.
scenes.caption: Researchers built a chamber with two compartments. The cell bodies of mouse sympathetic neurons sat in one compartment. Their axons grew through narrow grooves into the other. Many sympathetic neurons send branches toward targets that make NGF. Both sides held NGF, a trophic factor, which is a growth factor supplied by the target. This setup lets them remove NGF from the axons alone.

scenes.tts: First, remove N G F from the axons alone. The axons degenerate. The cell bodies live, because they still have N G F. This is the local route. This pruning needs three caspases: caspase nine, caspase three and caspase six. It does not need Apaf one. Keep that name in mind.
scenes.visual: NGF leaves the axon side; axons fragment and vanish; bodies live; three caspase chips appear; a crossed-out Apaf-1 chip.
scenes.caption: First, remove NGF from the axons alone. The axons degenerate. The cell bodies live, because they still have NGF. This is the local route. This pruning needs three caspases: caspase-9, caspase-3 and caspase-6. It does not need Apaf-1. Keep that name in mind.
scenes.narration: First, remove NGF from the axons alone. The axons degenerate. The cell bodies live, because they still have NGF. This is the local route. This pruning needs three caspases: caspase-9, caspase-3 and caspase-6. It does not need Apaf-1. Keep that name in mind.

scenes.tts: Now start again, and remove N G F from the whole dish. This time the neurons die. This is the whole-cell route. Their death needs Apaf one. Apaf one builds the apoptosome. The apoptosome is the usual activator of caspase nine in apoptosis. When N G F is removed from the whole dish, loss of caspase six no longer protects the axons.
scenes.visual: Fresh chamber; NGF leaves everywhere; neurons die; chain Apaf-1, apoptosome, caspase-9, neurons die; crossed caspase-6 chip.
scenes.caption: Now start again, and remove NGF from the whole dish. This time the neurons die. This is the whole-cell route. Their death needs Apaf-1. Apaf-1 builds the apoptosome. The apoptosome is the usual activator of caspase-9 in apoptosis. When NGF is removed from the whole dish, loss of caspase-6 no longer protects the axons.
scenes.narration: Now start again, and remove NGF from the whole dish. This time the neurons die. This is the whole-cell route. Their death needs Apaf-1. Apaf-1 builds the apoptosome. The apoptosome is the usual activator of caspase-9 in apoptosis. When NGF is removed from the whole dish, loss of caspase-6 no longer protects the axons.

scenes.tts: Now test the idea. Take Apaf one away from the neurons. Remove N G F from the axons alone. The axons still degenerate, and the cell bodies live. Now remove N G F from the whole dish. These neurons resist death. Without Apaf one, the whole-cell route is blocked. The whole-cell route needs Apaf one to activate caspase nine.
scenes.visual: Chamber with Apaf-1 removed: local removal still prunes axons; reset; whole-dish removal, neurons survive; Apaf-1 to caspase-9 link.
scenes.caption: Now test the idea. Take Apaf-1 away from the neurons. Remove NGF from the axons alone. The axons still degenerate, and the cell bodies live. Now remove NGF from the whole dish. These neurons resist death. Without Apaf-1, the whole-cell route is blocked. The whole-cell route needs Apaf-1 to activate caspase-9.
scenes.narration: Now test the idea. Take Apaf-1 away from the neurons. Remove NGF from the axons alone. The axons still degenerate, and the cell bodies live. Now remove NGF from the whole dish. These neurons resist death. Without Apaf-1, the whole-cell route is blocked. The whole-cell route needs Apaf-1 to activate caspase-9.

scenes.tts: The same caspases can be reached by two routes, one local and one global. The local route uses caspase nine, three and six, but not Apaf one. The whole-cell route needs the apoptosome. The routes share enzymes but are wired differently. X I A P and the proteasome guard the cell body. Remember: only the whole-cell route needs Apaf one.
scenes.visual: Two rows: local route (crossed Apaf-1, caspases, axons degenerate) and whole-cell route (Apaf-1, apoptosome, caspase-9, neurons die).
